traj.txt:
Based on the documents provided, the phrase "by the skin of your teeth" (or "skin of my teeth") originates from the **Bible**, specifically **Job 19:20** (Document [1]).

In the Book of Job, the character **Job** is the one speaking this line. Throughout the book (and specifically in Chapter 19), Job is **defending his innocence** and integrity against his friends (Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar) who argue that his suffering must be a result of his sin. He defends himself ("this stuff" referring to his righteousness/innocence) while describing how close he came to death ("escaped with the skin of my teeth").

While Document [7] mentions **Mike Godwin** as a "free speech lawyer" who wrote a book called *Cyber Rights* about "defending free speech," there is no evidence in the provided text linking him to the origin of the phrase "skin of my teeth." The phrase's origin is explicitly tied to Job in the Bible.
